title: Reach the Top 1% of Your Field (Deliberate Practice)
author: Scott Young
description: Revisiting one of the most influential theories of mastery and professional excellence. The post Reach the Top 1% of Your Field (Deliberate Practice) appeared first on Scott H Young .
summary: Few ideas have shaped my thinking about learning more than Anders Ericsson’s work on deliberate practice. He argued persuasively that quantity of practice goes a long way in explaining performance differences in fields like chess, music and athletics and, further, that certain types of practice are far more effective than others for learning.
takeaways: He argued persuasively that quantity of practice goes a long way in explaining performance differences in fields like chess, music and athletics and, further, that certain types of practice are far more effective than others for learning.

To me, this doesn’t undermine the more basic claims that a large quantity of practice is important for learning and that certain kinds of effortful/guided practice may be much more effective than simply spending hours performing the skill.
If expertise isn’t defined in terms of repeatable, superior performance according to an unbiased standard, then the study shifts from cognitive development to sociology.
